findings.reason: the population must be "every DD path that carries a domain", plus an account of the unclassified ones, or the evidence numerator overstates the classified set.
findings.text: s2 opens "Every DD path in the graph carries a physics domain from the build", but the build sets physics_domain = null for infrastructure paths (ids_properties/*, code/*) and records them as domain_source = 'none_metadata' (iter_codex/graph/dd_domain_classifier.py:330-355), so a whole-population claim will meet paths with no domain and no mechanism

findings.reason: the required count cannot be read from the record s2 describes, so the node will either invent a number or measure names while calling them paths.
findings.text: s2 requires "the count of paths whose domain rests on the IDS-to-domain table alone", but the IDS-to-domain table supplies candidate domains to a standard NAME through its sources' IDSes (iter_codex/standard_names/domain_decision.py:440, candidate_domains), while a DD path's domain_source records only jev_tree / llm_classified / deterministic_override / inherited_from_parent / none_metadata, with no IDS-table value

findings.reason: as ordered the table cannot be regenerated before s1 closes, so the node must either hand-edit generated data or deadlock; the order or an explicit dependency must change.
findings.text: s1's done-when requires codex's IDS-to-domain table to name only ruled values, but ids_domains.json is derived from IMASNode.physics_domain (iter_codex/ids/tools.py:344-374 query_ids_physics_domains) and the graph's path domains are only rerun in s3, which depends on s1

findings.reason: without a planted name the rerun's write path is never shown to fire, and an empty moved-path sample could pass vacuously.
findings.text: s3 declares no negative control: its predecessor sn-audited-group-release §6 required "a recorded run on a disposable graph shows one planted name moved to its ruled part and one planted name outside transport left where it was", and that planted control is absent here

findings.reason: naming the fragment path is what makes the evidence openable by a later reader and by the coordinator's hand read.
findings.text: s2 asks for "An evidence page and data file" and s3 for before/after counts and a hand-read sample, but neither names a durable path (the predecessor §6 named docs/evidence/fragments/sn-audited-group-release/), so a worker may leave the evidence in a session scratchpad or temporary directory

findings.reason: the blanket search either flags files the plan never intended to edit or forces rewriting vendored DD metadata; the search must name its scope or the exempt resources.
findings.text: s1's "A search of the package and the tests finds none of the three removed values" collides with vendored DD resources that carry computational_workflow as an assigned physics_domain (iter_codex/resources/imas_data_dictionary/4.1.1/schemas/detailed/workflow.json "physics_domain": "computational_workflow"), which are inputs, not codex definitions

findings.reason: the binding "Both imas-codex pins name the release candidate" is directly checkable in pyproject.toml, so the weak corroborating clause does not make the whole done-when unfailable.
findings.text: s1's "An environment synced from them reports the 30 values" is satisfied by the sibling editable source override (pyproject.toml [tool.uv.sources] imas-standard-names = { path = "../imas-standard-names", editable = true }) rather than by the pins, so the sync clause measures the sibling checkout, not the pins

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — each cited plan section and the evidence data file resolve; extensionless hrefs resolve as `<path>.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s2 asks for "the count of paths whose domain rests on the IDS-to-domain table alone", a record the build does not produce for paths; s2 and s3 also declare no negative control, s3 having dropped the planted-name disposable-graph control its predecessor required.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — s2 and s3 name no durable path for their evidence page, citable data file or readback, so a worker may write to a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose reaches a code symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s2's premise that every DD path carries a physics domain is contradicted by the build's own record; and s1's blanket package search collides with vendored DD resource metadata.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable; s1's pin update is part of adopting the vocabulary.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — s1 requires the IDS-to-domain table to carry ruled values, but that table's values are derived from IMASNode.physics_domain and are only rerun by s3, which depends on s1.
